A narrow vertical strip of shifting colour bands with no legible content, on the Acknowledgements page; appears to be a decorative sidebar divider rather than an informative graphic. Content beyond the colour bands could not be determined from the extracted image.
A photograph, on the Executive summary page, of a group of six boys sitting together outdoors against a brick wall, most looking at a red mobile phone held by one boy in the centre of the group.

A photograph, on the Introduction page, of two women sitting closely together in conversation outdoors against a whitewashed stone wall: one in a green-and-black patterned headscarf, the other in a yellow headscarf holding an infant wrapped in a peach-coloured blanket, with a small mobile phone visible in the first woman's hand.

A narrow vertical strip of shifting colour bands with no legible content, on the Background: scaling up mHealth page; appears to be a decorative sidebar divider rather than an informative graphic. Content beyond the colour bands could not be determined from the extracted image.

A photograph, on the AXIS 1 Groundwork section-opening page, of a sleeping infant seated in a camouflage-patterned chair beside an adult's hand holding a pink mobile phone displaying an SMS text message (in Vietnamese, referencing bringing the child to a health station for vaccination on a given date).

A diagram titled 'DETERMINANT LAYERS OF UHC' showing horizontal coverage bars grouped by category (Cost: Financial coverage; Quality: Effective coverage; Demand: Continuous coverage, Contact coverage; Supply: Accessibility of health facilities, Availability of human resources, Availability of commodities and equipment; Accountability: Accountability coverage, Target population, Total population). Each of the top eight bars ends in a lettered circle (A-H) connected by a dotted line, representing the current performance gap, to a vertical red bar labelled 'TARGET: universal effective coverage of health interventions of known efficacy'. A side panel titled 'mHEALTH STRATEGIES' lists, for each letter, the mHealth applications that can close that gap: H - Mobile financial transactions; G - Decision support, POC diagnostics, Telemedicine, Reminders, Incentives; F - Persistent electronic health records, Provider-to-provider communication, Work planning, Reminders; E - Behavior change communication (BCC), Incentives; D - Hotlines, Client mobile apps, Client information content subscriptions; C - Human resource management, Provider training, Telemedicine; B - Supply management, Counterfeit prevention; A - Client registration, Electronic medical records, Unique identifiers, Data collection and reporting, Screening tools, Civil registration and vital events. A legend below explains the dotted line as the current gap in determinant performance, the circle-and-arrow as illustrative mHealth strategies to close performance gaps, and a dashed vertical line as the minimum performance of the supply determinant.

A screenshot of the mHealth Working Group online discussion platform, showing a navigation bar (Home, Discussions, Library, Calendar), a filter set to 'Last modified', and a list of discussion thread previews with poster names, dates and brief excerpts, including topics on solar chargers for tablets, CommCare webinars, and a USAID/ASH mHealth Compendium release.
A photograph of two people seated outdoors on wooden chairs in a shaded, tree-lined setting, engaged in conversation; one wears a light-coloured hat and shirt, the other a pink headwrap.

The cover of the JSI publication 'The Pathway to Supply Chain Sustainability: A Planning Tool for Scaling & Institutionalizing Innovations within Public Sector Supply Chains', showing the JSI logo at the top and a row of small human figures below the title.

The cover of the guide 'How to Approach mHealth' (Introduction to mHealth series, prepared by Kelly Keisling), showing a photograph of a woman in a clinic setting and a short descriptive paragraph beneath the title.

The cover of the WHO-ITU publication 'National eHealth Strategy Toolkit', showing a world map overlaid with a glowing heartbeat/pulse line and a stethoscope icon, with the WHO and ITU logos at the bottom.

The cover of 'Information and Communication Technologies for Women's and Children's Health: A Planning Workbook', showing three photographs of women and children in community/clinical settings above the title and a row of partner organization logos along the bottom.

A screenshot of the K4Health 'Toolkits' website header and the landing page for 'The mHealth Planning Guide: Key Considerations for Integrating Mobile Technology into Health Programs', including the site navigation bar and a photograph of a woman using a mobile phone.

The cover of a GSMA 'Mobile for Development' country feasibility report, titled 'mHealth Country Feasibility Report: Mozambique', with the GSMA logo and a geometric pattern of teal and grey diamond shapes on a white background.

A thumbnail of a HealthEnabled African Digital Dashboard, a one-page infographic-style country profile with a map of Africa, coloured text boxes and small charts summarizing national eHealth policy and deployment information; individual text within the thumbnail is too small to read and could not be determined from the extracted image.

A photograph of two women seated indoors wearing matching bright blue saris, heads bent together looking at a mobile phone one of them holds, with papers and folders on the floor in front of them. Illustrates the AXIS 2 Partnerships section.

A narrow vertical strip of colour bands (blue, orange and black) with no legible content; appears to be a decorative sidebar divider rather than an informative graphic. Content beyond the colour bands could not be determined from the extracted image.

A photograph of two people, one wearing a red shirt and the other a headscarf and carrying a shoulder bag, walking away from the camera along a dirt path through green vegetation, with a dog visible on the path between them.

A photograph of a wall or board covered with handwritten sticky notes in yellow and blue, arranged in a grid, used for a brainstorming or planning exercise; individual note text is too small to be read and could not be determined from the extracted image.
A photograph of a man seated at a desk working through stacks of papers and binders, with a mobile phone and notice board visible in the background.

The cover of 'Information and Communication Technologies for Women's and Children's Health: A Planning Workbook', showing three photographs of women and children in community/clinical settings above the title and a row of partner organization logos along the bottom (same publication cover as shown earlier in the document).

The cover of the WHO/UNICEF guide 'A practical guide for engaging with mobile network operators in mHealth for reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health', showing the WHO and UNICEF logos, the title, and a background pattern of connected dots evoking a mobile network, with a photograph of a hand holding a mobile phone in the lower right.

The cover/first page of the contract-management brief 'Fifty Tips for Your Statement of Work', laid out as a two-column reference sheet with a 'Back to Basics' banner; body text is too small to be read and could not be determined from the extracted image.

The cover of a situation-analysis report titled 'ICT4SOML: Leveraging ICTs to Save the Lives of One Million Women and Children in Nigeria', dated 11 February 2015, showing the logos of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Federal Ministry of Health, mHealth Alliance, Intel and GSMA.

The cover of the GSMA mWomen publication 'Mutual Value, Mutual Gain: Best practices from successful social sector partnerships with mobile network operators', showing a photograph of several smiling women and the GSMA mWomen logo.

The cover of 'Scaling Up Mobile Health: Developing mHealth Partnerships for Scale' (Advanced Development for Africa), illustrated with a stylized tree whose branches are coloured lines connecting numbered circular icons, symbolizing a network of partnerships.

A photograph of a mobile money or phone top-up kiosk: a woman in the foreground reaches across a wooden counter to hand cash to a seated attendant visible through a wooden serving window; a small device resembling a mobile-money terminal, a basic mobile phone and a paper ledger sit on the counter between them. Illustrates the AXIS 3 Financial health section.

A narrow vertical strip of shifting colour bands (blue, orange, green tones) with no legible content, on the AXIS 3 Financial health thematic-overview page; appears to be a decorative sidebar divider rather than an informative graphic. Content beyond the colour bands could not be determined from the extracted image.

A photograph of two hands holding a smartphone displaying a Vietnamese-language mobile app screen with a bulleted menu, held over an open paper patient register ruled into columns (including headings for name, date of birth, vaccinations such as DPT/VGB-HB, and remarks).

A financial 'COST MODEL' table with columns for Data Type, per user/CHC per month, per user/CHC per year, and All users/CHCs per month, per year and pilot. Rows cover categories such as Incoming SMS, Outgoing SMS (with sub-items for reminders and query responses to patients and nurses), GPRS usage in KB (patient encounter forms, error exchanges, nurse queries), and Voice minutes incoming and outgoing (patient-provider messages, call centre registrations, nurse and user support). A highlighted TOTAL COST row gives per-month/per-year/pilot figures of 3,522 / 42,262 / 44,998. A bottom 'Assumptions' section gives the average cost per SMS (incoming and outgoing) in GHS and USD.

The cover of the report 'Sustainable Financing for Mobile Health (mHealth): Options and opportunities for mHealth financial models in low and middle-income countries', published by mHealth Alliance and Vital Wave Consulting, illustrated with a collage of small photographs of people using mobile devices.

A CommCare-branded spreadsheet costing tool showing a 'Scale of Operations' section with rows for number of CHWs using CommCare and number of people reached per CHW across five years, an 'Additional staff and office needed for CommCare' section with unit counts, and the start of a 'Detailed projected costs' table with unit types, numbers of units and cost per unit for annual training days by CHW, project manager and field staff roles.

The cover of the report 'Preparing the Next Generation of Community Health Workers: The Power of Technology for Training' (Dalberg Global Development Advisors, May 2012), showing a pattern of small house-shaped icons above the title and a row of supporting-organization logos, including Dalberg, at the bottom.

A blank Business Model Canvas template: a grid of nine labelled boxes for Key Partners, Key Activities, Value Propositions, Customer Relationships, Customer Segments, Key Resources, Channels, Cost Structure and Revenue Streams, each marked with a small icon, with blank fields at the top for designer name and date.
The cover of the book 'Business Model Generation', showing the title in large text on a textured dark background with small credit text below.
The cover of the book 'Value Proposition Design', showing the title beside a colourful illustration of stacked geometric blocks and small figures with a target/bullseye icon.

A photograph of two hands holding a smartphone displaying a Swahili-language data-entry or assessment app screen with a question ('Chunguza mpauko wa kiganja cha mkono') and a selectable option ('Kawaida'); a second basic mobile phone with a green charging cable is visible on the table in the background. Illustrates the AXIS 4 Technology & architecture section.

A photograph inside a home showing a sleeping infant in a green hammock with pink cushions on the left, while two men sit cross-legged on a woven mat, one operating a mobile phone while the other looks on; a printed document lies on the mat in front of them.
A photograph of a small group of people, including children, seated together on patterned floor cushions, gathered around and looking at a tablet held by one member of the group.
A photograph of a pregnant woman standing outdoors, looking down at a mobile phone she holds in both hands, with trees and cleared brush in the background.
A close-up photograph of two hands holding a smartphone displaying a green-and-white messaging or list interface; a second person's arm is visible blurred in the background.

A screenshot of API documentation for a facility registry. It shows a section on the internal system id with an example 'id:' value and a note that the API does not enforce a specific ID format; a URL section giving an example REST endpoint for a facility resource (http://facilityregistry.org/api/v1/facilities/...); and an 'External Facility Identifiers' section explaining that each external identifier consists of an agency (who created the code), a context (the system in which the agency uses the code, e.g. HMIS, DHIS2, HR) and an id, followed by an example JSON array of identifier objects.

The cover/summary sheet 'Principles for Digital Development', laid out as a poster with the title at the top and several numbered principles arranged in a grid of short text blocks below; individual principle text is too small to be read and could not be determined from the extracted image.

A screenshot of the CommCare Help web page 'Choosing a Device Type', showing the page header, a bulleted list of topic links (Android or Feature Phone; Android Phone or Tablet for Android project), and the beginning of body text comparing feature phones and Android devices.

The cover of the report 'Patient Privacy in a Mobile World: A Framework to Address Privacy Law Issues in Mobile Health' (TrustLaw, dated June 2013), showing a close-up photograph of a patient's face with an ECG electrode attached to the forehead, and several sponsor logos along the bottom.
The logo of the 'dhis2 Academy', consisting of the text 'dhis2' in white on a blue background with 'Academy' beneath it.

A title slide/graphic for 'Open Concept Lab: Open Source Terminology Management for Health Interoperability', with a subtitle 'Maternal Health Use Case' and simple line-drawn figures of two people beside icons of a clipboard and a computer, and the Open Concept Lab logo.

The cover of the report 'The State of Standards and Interoperability for mHealth among Low- and Middle-Income Countries' by Jonathan D. Payne, mHealth Alliance, dated March 2013, showing a photograph of a mother and child in the lower portion of the cover.
The OpenHIE logo, showing a stylized circular icon made of overlapping teal, blue, orange and green dots beside the wordmark 'OpenHIE'.

The cover of the 'eHealth Strategy South Africa' document, showing a stylized globe icon formed from glowing dots and lines on an orange background, with the National Department of Health logo and tagline.

A photograph inside a clinic office showing four staff members in white coats/uniforms: one woman seated at a desk on the left, a standing man pointing toward a window while resting his hand on the back of a chair, a seated woman holding an open folder, and another seated woman typing at a desktop computer. Illustrates the AXIS 5 Operations section.
A photograph of two women seated indoors, one wearing a red top pointing at a tablet held by the other, who wears glasses and a black top, illustrating hands-on training with a mobile device.

A photograph of two people seated on wooden chairs outdoors near a house with a banana tree in the background; one, wearing a cap, writes on papers held on their lap while the other, in a headscarf and patterned dress, looks on.

A photograph of a woman in a colourful patterned dress carrying a blue container, walking along a dirt path past a large pile of harvested produce, with a house and another person visible in the background.

A screenshot of a printed device-use agreement headed with a declaration that the signer has received a handset and accessories from the Ghana Health Service. It is organized into numbered sections — Ownership, Use, Maintenance, and Loss and Theft — each containing several numbered clauses; for example, the Loss and Theft section specifies that loss must be reported immediately, describes a cost-sharing formula between the user (75%) and the Ghana Health Service (25%) for replacement due to negligence, and sets out penalties for repeated negligent loss.
A photograph looking into an open cardboard shipping box packed with stacked mobile phone boxes in blue and green packaging, with phones visible through some of the open boxes.

The cover of the report 'Mobile Technology for Community Health in Ghana' (subtitled with reference to lessons learned so far), showing a photograph of a woman in colourful dress with a child, and the Grameen Foundation and MOTECH logos at the top.

A screenshot of a CommCare Help page titled 'Mobile User Survey Templates', with the CommCare HELP logo and body text organized under headings Purpose, Use, Training (one-time or periodic), Ongoing, Built-in, and Types of Surveys.
The ORB logo: the letters 'ORB' in white inside a solid dark blue circle.

A photograph of a person seen from behind, silhouetted against a computer monitor displaying a RapidSMS Rwanda web report ('NATION WIDE, 01/SEP/2013 - 19/SEP/2013') with browser tabs for Google Translate, RapidSMS Rwanda and related pages. The visible table has columns for Location, Type, Reporter and Patient, with rows recording community health worker reports such as 'Community Based Nutrition', 'Pregnancy' and 'Community Case Management' from locations including Rukoma, Jarama and Gishari. Illustrates the AXIS 6 Monitoring & evaluation section.

A photograph of hands writing on a paper form on a desk, with a desktop computer monitor in the background displaying a data-entry webpage with a blue highlighted button; a printer sits beside the monitor.

A photograph of a hand pointing at a computer monitor displaying a data table with multiple columns and rows of records; individual column headings and values are too small to be read and could not be determined from the extracted image.

The cover of the 'MAMA Research Agenda' report (Mobile Alliance for Maternal Action, dated 2015), showing the MAMA logo at the top and a photograph of a group of women in colourful saris standing together, with the subtitle 'Research Agenda' below.

The cover of the World Bank book 'Impact Evaluation in Practice' by Paul J. Gertler, Sebastian Martinez, Patrick Premand, Laura B. Rawlings and Christel M. J. Vermeersch, with the title in large text on a white background bordered by a row of small circular dot icons.

A screenshot of the header of the mHealthEvidence.org website (by K4Health), showing the site logo with a magnifying glass icon, a 'Translate' link, a 'mHealth Evidence Taxonomy' link, 'Sign in' and 'Register' buttons, and a 'Go to...' search/navigation dropdown.
